_comment: Carry destination for the round-5 governance/record findings (#1301, R5-D11-02
and #1303, R5-D13-01). Round 5 filed 48 findings as #1293-#1340 and no umbrella
issue of its own, so the destination is #201 -- the audit programme's standing
tracking issue, the one that received round 5's own round-end comment -- and no
roster group in this tree claims it. Shape and required fields:
stage: any later seat that stamps a release (tools/release/stamp.py, the deploy-key tag push of docs/decisions/0009 step 5); the D13 dimension of a later audit round (tools/audit/briefs/D13.md is its method, tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py its harness); and the D11 dimension of a later audit round, whose method tools/audit/briefs/D11.md is and whose subject is .github/workflows/governance.yml

carries.from: the round-5 D11-02 finding (#1301), whose fix is rule "rows" in tools/release/stamp.py -- the stamp now re-applies `record`'s own predicate to the window it is about to close
carries.control: The window `<last v* tag>..origin/main` is the window `record` reads, and the tag push is main-protect's only bypass, so one stamp can carry every rowless merge behind the new tag out of every future window at once. Established by measurement, not argument: the finding's harness (tools/audit/round5/D11/seat-b/corpus_churn.py) reads the same counts at origin/main before this fix and at this fix's head, and the number that matters is the INSTRUMENT's, not the harness's -- `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --check` exits 0 over a window whose merges are minutes old, because at stamp time every merge is PENDING and `--check` refuses only OVERDUE and UNCHECKED; the new `--require-rows` exits 1 over the same ledger and names the rowless merges. The perturbation that would have voided it: a row added for one window merge moves the count by exactly one. The fix is measurement-neutral by construction -- corpus_churn.py prints byte-identical RESULT lines at the pre-fix and post-fix heads, which is the null control separating `--require-rows` (reading the ledger under a stricter bar) from a change to the ledger itself.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --check` and `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --require-rows` over the same tree, then `python3 tools/audit/round5/D11/seat-b/corpus_churn.py`. They agree on every verdict but PENDING, and that single disagreement is the whole finding; a later round that reads them as the same predicate has re-derived the escape.
carries.brief: Stamp-time precondition, not an opportunity: `tools/release/stamp.py` REFUSES to stamp when any merged pull request in the window it would close has no disposition row, and the only override is the explicit `--allow-rowless` flag, which prints the instrument's own output before proceeding. The rows it demands are the ones `record` demands, on the same two surfaces tests/delivery_status.py's DISPOSITION_FILES names. A stamp over a rowless window is no longer an ordinary release step: it is a knowingly deferred batch, and it is recorded as one. The re-application lives in the stamp's module docstring as rule "rows", so a seat that reads the contract rather than the flag sees it before it runs.

carries.from: the round-5 D13-01 finding (#1303), whose fix makes the CFR exclusion list a registered in-tree artifact that the instrument reads from the repository root, failing closed when it is absent
carries.control: The finding: the round-5 harness opened `cfr_exclusions.json` beside itself, so `cfr_excluded` came from a file the tree did not carry -- and tools/audit/briefs/D13.md asks for `a JSON file beside policy_budgets.json that your first round creates with a reason per job`. Established by measurement at both ends in a clone at the round's baseline: with the sibling list and the tree holding no list, the harness prints cfr_excluded=0.0; with the artifact registered at .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json and the sibling removed, it prints the identical eight-merge numbers, which is the null control that shows the re-point moved the citation and not the metric. The perturbation the brief names still moves the number by exactly the excluded job's head count: `EXCLUSION_DROP=record` takes cfr_excluded 0.0 -> 1.0, record's eight of eight heads. And the fail-closed arm: with the artifact removed the harness raises, naming the registered path, rather than silently excluding nobody -- which is the always-green shape a metric `retaken minus the by-design reds` degrades into.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: run the D13 instrument (tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py) with its fixtures, then again with EXCLUSION_DROP naming the excluded job. If the second run's cfr_excluded does not move by that job's head count, the list is not being read. Then `python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.load(open('.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json'))['excluded_jobs']))"` -- the list is a narrowing of the metric, so a round that GROWS it is making a deliberate edit, and an unjustified entry hides a real change failure rather than a by-design one.
carries.brief: Constraint on how the exclusion list is carried: it is ONE registered artifact at `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json`, a top-level object with an `excluded_jobs` map keyed by check-run name beside a `_comment`, in the shape .claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json takes. The instrument resolves it against the REPOSITORY, not against the seat, and raises when the map is missing or empty -- so a later round does not create a second list under a name of its choosing, and does not publish an un-excluded rate under the excluded rate's name. Each entry carries the reason and the citation it rests on; the one entry at the round-5 values is `record`, and the reason a later round must re-check rather than assume is that the red is by design only while the batch interval holds.

carries.from: the round-6 D11-02 finding (#1403), whose fix adds the `Restore the check source from the base commit` step to the `policy-docs` job of .github/workflows/governance.yml and the entry-point exit-status arm to .claude/workflows/policy_lint_mutants.mjs
carries.control: The assumption before this fix was that a required context which grades the policy corpus runs the corpus's own checker. It did not: `policy-docs` checked out no `ref:`, so the program grading the corpus was the pull request's copy of it. Established by measurement at both ends in a worktree of the fix's head whose only differences were a corpus defect (one line of CLAUDE.md citing a file the tree does not carry, line count unchanged) and a one-line mutation of the checker's exit status -- `process.exit(errors > 0 || rc ? 1 : 0)` gated on `process.env.POLICY_LINT_TEMPLATE`, which is the shape that evades the gate's own witness. Before the fix, that tree's `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` exited 0 while printing `ERROR [citations] CLAUDE.md:20` and `ERROR [index]`, its stdout byte-identical to the unmutated checker's, and the base's mutation lane exited 0 as well; the acceptance's template arms in tests/entities.py, which empty the checker and demand a red, returned 1 and 0. After the fix, on the same tree: the lane exits 1 naming the exit status, and the required context's own command exits 1 naming the corpus defect once the pin has run, the pin reporting one file differing from the pull request's copy. The null control runs both ways: on the healthy tree at the same head the pin restores nothing and the lint stays at 0, and with the pinned ref equal to the head -- the push-to-main shape, where the step reads `github.sha` -- the checkout is a no-op over a clean tree.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: apply the same two perturbations (a corpus defect that does not change a line count, and an exit status that does not track the findings), then run the job's own commands in this order -- `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint_mutants.mjs` must exit nonzero naming the exit status; `git checkout <base> -- '.claude/workflows/*.mjs' '.claude/workflows/*.py' '.claude/workflows/vendor'` must print a count you can read; `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs` must exit 1 with your corpus defect named. Require both ends: on the healthy tree each of those is 0, and a pin whose checkout silently matched nothing would leave the mutated checker in place and print a count of zero. Then check the three shapes the pin does not cover, each a candidate finding rather than a refutation: a criteria edit, a checker added as a module beside the pinned programs, and a program edited together with the self-test lane that drives it.
carries.brief: Constraint on any seat adding a corpus check or moving a step in the `policy-docs` job of .github/workflows/governance.yml. (1) A corpus check is a function inside .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs, named in that file's own lists of check names, never a module beside it: the new step restores the `.mjs` and `.py` programs under .claude/workflows/ plus .claude/workflows/vendor from the base commit, and a file the base does not carry cannot be restored, so a checker added as its own module stays the pull request's own and the corpus is graded by the copy under test -- the defect of #1403 in its original shape. (2) The job now has two halves and that step is the boundary. The five steps above it -- .claude/workflows/policy_lint_mutants.mjs, the `--self-test` runs of .claude/workflows/fragments_sync.mjs and tools/audit/record-predicate/sweep.mjs, the `--hooks` run of .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs and the `self-test` run of .claude/workflows/gh_comment.py -- drive the PULL REQUEST's programs on purpose, because a self-test that ran the base's copy would report on neither; every step below it grades the pull request's data with the base's programs. Moving a step across that boundary silently changes which side of it a check is on. (3) The pin covers programs, not criteria: .claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json, .claude/workflows/policy_known_bad.json, .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json and the sync surface .claude/workflows/fragments_sync.mjs checks against .claude/workflows/web-fragments.md stay the pull request's, because a fixture's expected outcome has to be the data under test. Those three places -- a criteria file, a checker outside the restored paths, and the self-test block above the step -- are where the pull request's own copy is still what runs, and that is where a later round hunting this class of defect should look.

carries.from: the pull request fixing the round-6 D13-03 finding (#1407), which makes the round-4 DORA instrument (tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py, `cfr_keyings`) report the change-failure rate at BOTH keyings -- at the merge commit, where `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json` acts, and at the pull-request head, where a merge is gated -- and pins the pair in tests/entities.py
carries.control: The finding: the exclusion list's single entry `record` fails at 58 of the 67 merge commits in the window v6.6.0..e336cc2c and is SKIPPED at every one of the 67 pull-request heads, because its workflow gates the job to the non-pull_request event. So excluding it moves the merge-keyed rate 0.925 -> 0.09 and leaves the head-keyed rate at 0.134 -- the rate at the surface a merge is actually gated on, unchanged. Established by measurement at both ends: the instrument prints the un-excluded rate beside the excluded one from the same call over the same maps, so the exclusion's own delta is visible on each keying, and it is 56 merges at the merge keying and zero at the head keying; the round-6 finder harness measured the same figures, so the tracked instrument reproduces them rather than restating them. The perturbation that would have voided it: the names failing at the HEAD are `nightly-status` (7 of the 67) and `delivery-status` (2 of the 67), so one entry added for either moves the head keying and the pair stops separating the two surfaces. The key-set null control tests/entities.py already holds -- `excluded_jobs` is exactly the set holding `record`, with the gate jobs absent -- is what refuses that entry.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base, run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py` and read `cfr_merge_keyed` beside `cfr_head_keyed`; both are RESULT lines the instrument prints, and `cfr_exclusions` is printed with them so the list a rate came from is on the same screen. Or run tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py with `EXCLUSION_DROP=record`, which moves the merge-keyed rate by that job's head count. A rate reported at one keying only, or an entry added for a name that fails at the head, is this finding re-derived. The instrument pins its window (`D13_SINCE` / `D13_HEAD`), so a re-take names its own baseline instead of tracking a moving main.
carries.brief: Constraint on every change-failure rate a later round reports: the rate is TWO numbers -- the merge-keyed rate and the pull-request-head-keyed rate -- printed together and never one alone, because `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json` narrows only the merge keying while a merge is gated on the head keying. The artifact's `_keying` field states that rule for whoever edits the list, and tools/audit/briefs/D13.md's DORA item asks for the list without naming a keying, which is how the single-number report arose. A check-run name that fails at the pull-request head is a real gate red: it must NOT be added to the list, however much it costs the merge keying, and a report that names such a name as excluded is the escape this carry closes.

carries.from: the pull request fixing the round-7 D13-06 finding (#1476), which makes the same round-4 DORA instrument report the rate PER CHECK-RUN NAME at both keyings (tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py, `cfr_by_name`), and records `mutation` in .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json's new `not_excluded` map as a name deliberately NOT on the list
carries.control: The finding: the carry above settles that the rate is two numbers, but two aggregates still do not say WHICH name separates them, and over the round-7 window the whole separation is one name. `mutation` fails 4 of the window's 31 merge commits and 0 of its 31 pull-request heads, so it is the entire 0.129 between the merge-keyed rate (0.226) and the head-keyed one (0.129) -- invisible in either published figure, and the reason a reader cannot tell a merge-surface red from a head-surface one. Established by measurement at both ends: `cfr_by_name` prints the pair `[merge, head]` for every name failing at EITHER surface, over the same maps `cfr_keyings` aggregates, so the four names other than `mutation` that fail at the merge keying print [0.032, 0.0] apiece and `delivery-status` prints the mirror [0.0, 0.129]. The perturbation that would have voided it: adding one name to the exclusion list IN MEMORY moves the merge-keyed rate by exactly that name's count and leaves the head-keyed rate where it was -- `mutation` 0.226 -> 0.097 while the head keying stays 0.129 -- which is the arithmetic statement that it is a merge-surface red. The null control is the key set: a name failing at neither surface (`record`, 0 of 31 here) is ABSENT from the map rather than a zero row, so the map's keys are compared as a set and never as a total.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base, run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py` and read the `cfr_by_name` RESULT beside `cfr_merge_keyed` / `cfr_head_keyed`; the per-name pairs must sum to the aggregate keyings over the same window, and any name whose pair is nonzero at one surface only is a candidate the list owner must judge. Then `python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.load(open('.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json'))['excluded_jobs']))"` -- it must still be exactly `['record']`. A round that reports a single per-name number, or that finds `mutation` (or `nightly-status`, or `delivery-status`) added to `excluded_jobs`, has re-derived this finding or the one above it.
carries.brief: Constraint on how a later round reports the change-failure rate: per-name at both keyings, BESIDE the two aggregates and never instead of them. Two aggregate rates hide which name separates the surfaces, and here the whole difference is one name -- and the instrument cannot decide whether that name's merge-surface red is a change failure at all. `mutation` fails 4 of the window's 31 merge commits (two pairs merged 4-5 s apart, i.e. two batch merges) where neither pull request's own head failed it, because the lane's inventory is the TREE (`tests/mutation_table.py`'s `unpinned_sites`) and on a push to `main` its scoping base IS `HEAD`, so a batch's merged tree can red it where no head did. Nothing in the finding says the red is spurious; it says whether a merge-surface red on a batch-merged tree is a change failure is the exclusion list owner's judgement, and it is recorded rather than made: `mutation` stays off the list, and .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json's `not_excluded` map carries the reason and the citation so the next reader meets the answer in the artifact rather than in a merged pull request's comments. Adding it to `excluded_jobs` is the same deliberate edit as growing the list, and owes the same justification.

carries.from: the seam the R7-INSTR-01 fix (#1477) returned when tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh was run as its own generator control: at this tree's merge base the script REFUSES to prepare a baseline for every round number except 4, so the documented way to prepare a round is inoperative for the next round
carries.control: The script's `finders_can_start` step refuses when a file a `tests/*.py` script hands to `Path(...)` or `open()` exists in the source checkout but not in the tree it just prepared, and `strip_earlier_rounds` deletes every `tools/audit/round*` except the round being prepared. Two files under `tools/audit/round4/` are read that way by tests/entities.py -- `Path("tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.json")` and `Path("tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py")`, added 2026-09-19 (a7d97d20) and 2026-09-20 (cd4b1927) -- while the refusal itself dates from round 4 (c68259b8, 2026-09-12). Each was harmless alone; together, any preparation whose round is not 4 drops files the HEAD tests open, and the script refuses after creating the worktrees and before writing any BASELINE.md. Established by measurement, not argument: in a throwaway clone of this tree's merge base, `PYTHON=<interp> bash tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh 98 6e2a0f2a` and the same script with this fix applied at round 99 both print `refusing: the preparation dropped file(s) a tests/*.py script opens unguarded: tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.json`, while the SAME script at round 4 completes -- `RESULT finders_can_start=ok` for the export and all five worktrees -- which is the control separating the round-from-4 strip from the environment. The rounds since have been prepared by hand (round 6's tools/audit/round6/BASELINE.md is hand-written and round 7's D13 was dispatched by hand), so this is a latent cost rather than a stopped programme.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base, in a scratch clone so the worktrees and the export land outside this repository: `git clone --depth 1 --no-single-branch file://<this checkout> /tmp/pb && cd /tmp/pb && PYTHON=$(command -v python3) bash tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh 98 $(git rev-parse HEAD)`. A refusal naming `tools/audit/round4/...` is this seam re-derived; then run it at round 4 and require it to complete, which is what says the refusal is about the strip and not about your clone. Two questions are open and belong to whoever holds the audit wall rather than to a fixer: whether the strip should exempt a file a HEAD test reads unguarded, or whether those two tests should read the register through a path that survives a round's preparation. Do not settle it by widening `finders_can_start` -- the refusal is the half that catches a preparation dropping a file by accident, and it is the only guard there.
carries.brief: Constraint on preparing the NEXT round's baseline: running `tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh <round> <sha>` for any round other than 4 refuses at this tree, after creating the worktrees and before writing any BASELINE.md, and the refusal is correct about its own predicate -- the prepared tree really does lack two files tests/entities.py opens unguarded, so a finder in it would die at import before its first measurement. Prepare the round deliberately instead of around the script: either carry the two `tools/audit/round4/` files into the export and the worktrees (the wall's rule is that earlier rounds must not STEER a finder, and a file a test reads is not steering), or re-point those two tests at a path that survives. Then take what #1477 fixed as given -- D13 is a dimension of the schedule in .claude/workflows/audit-find.js and needs a worktree rather than the export -- and keep the two lists it shares with this file's ISOLATED_DIMS in step, which .claude/workflows/check-wave-script.mjs now derives and refuses to see drift.

carries.from: the v6.7.8 stamp hotfix (the pull request repairing main's red entities check after the stamp commit), whose fix restores the may-drift entry R9-F2.3 (#1723) suspended for its wood_coil claim -- which the stamp deleted without restoring -- and moves the R8-P3 coverage ruling into tests/env_drift.py's may_drift_coverage_error, executed by --claims-only
carries.control: Established by measurement at both ends. At the stamp head, tests/entities.py's own check failed with uncovered ['wood_coil'] while the stamp's claims self-check had printed 'claims hygiene: HEAD^1 ok' -- the stamp's self-check DOES exec `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only HEAD^1` on the post-stamp tree, but --claims-only carried the scope rule (entries within MAY_DRIFT_ALLOWED, no name both claimed and may-drift) and not the coverage rule (every allowed name is may-drift or claimed for THIS VERSION), so a claim deleted by the stamp left its suspended entry covered by nothing. With the fix, the same --claims-only invocation on the broken tree refuses with MAY-DRIFT UNCOVERED naming wood_coil and exits 1, which publish_stamp treats as a refusal: undo_local_stamp discards the stamp commit before anything is pushed. The perturbation that would have voided it: re-suspending the entry at the fix head reproduces the refusal, restoring it returns exit 0. The null control: on the healthy tree the added rule changes no verdict -- claims hygiene stays ok -- because a tree whose may-drift list is complete satisfies the coverage rule by construction.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only <ref>` on a tree whose claim file suspends a may-drift entry for a claim that is absent or stamped for another VERSION must exit 1 with MAY-DRIFT UNCOVERED naming that entry; restoring the entry verbatim (or carrying the claim for the tree's own VERSION) must exit 0. Before running tools/release/stamp.py over a main whose claim file carries a suspension note, restore every suspended entry verbatim -- the note's own text carries the line -- or the stamp's self-check will discard the commit after making it.
carries.brief: Stamp-time precondition, not an opportunity: a stamp that empties the claim list owes every suspended may-drift entry back, verbatim, because a name may leave the may-drift list only while THIS release claims it (the R8-P3 ruling, option (a)) and the claim the suspension was made for expires with the stamp. The obligation is enforced, not advisory -- tools/release/stamp.py's claims self-check execs `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only HEAD^1` on the post-stamp tree and undo_local_stamp discards the commit on refusal -- so a stamping seat that misses the restore loses only the stamp run, never main's green. A suspension note in the claim file is a promise to a human; the coverage rule is the same promise made to the instrument, and the second is the one that refuses.

carries.from: PR #1879 (tools: programme instruments live in the tree, and a check refuses temp paths), whose tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py runs in governance.yml's non-grading instrument-self-tests job rather than in a required one
carries.control: Established by measurement at both ends. With tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py run in the wave-script job (a grading, required job) and tools/audit/seat/ unowned (tvofi, 2026-10-03: audit instruments are not code-owned), `python3 -I tools/audit/round6/D11/fix/codeowners_gap.py --check` refused it as UNCOVERED (uncovered_files=1); moved to instrument-self-tests, whose env sets HPO_JOB_GRADES: nothing, the same command reports uncovered_files=0 and tags it NO-PR-JOB. The null control: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, run in that same job from the start, was never reported uncovered. tmp_paths.py --check itself refuses 14 lines at origin/main 20f597c6 and 0 at the PR head, so the check works; only its gate status is weaker than a required grader's.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: `git cat-file -e <base>:tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py` must succeed before any job can restore it from the base; then add it to a pinned job's `git checkout "$PINNED" --` list in .github/workflows/governance.yml, declare it in .claude/workflows/field_coverage.mjs's DECLARED map (that program is pinned, so the declaration must already be on main when the pin lands), and run `python3 -I tools/audit/round6/D11/fix/codeowners_gap.py --check` (must report it PINNED, uncovered_files=0), `node .claude/workflows/field_coverage.mjs` (FIELD COVERAGE ok) and `bash tools/audit/prepr.sh` (its pinned-graders step names a local path for it).
carries.brief: Owed follow-up, two pull requests after #1879 merges: make tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py a pinned grader in a required governance.yml job, so a temp or machine path in a tracked script, workflow or decision record turns a required context red rather than the non-required instrument-self-tests. Step one declares it in .claude/workflows/field_coverage.mjs's DECLARED map (pinned, so it must land first); step two restores it from the base in a required job and runs `--check` there. It must not be made code-owned to get there: the owner ruled that audit instruments carry no owner, and decision 0013 stands unamended. Until both land, a red instrument-self-tests at a head is still a red check pr-contract makes the body answer, and tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py stops on it because it is not on the train's ignore list.

carries.from: RCA stale-pins (PR #2073, dev/audit/rca/R9-RCA-stale-pins.md): the frozen fixture tools/policy/fixtures/wave-1b-931dffe.json, pinned by REQUIRED_931DFFE's `wood_share:1152` entry in tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs, which requires a path:line (anchored) ERROR naming thermal_model.py:1152 and so depends on the production file's line layout
carries.control: Established by measurement at both ends, with its null control, on origin/main 47b083b0. Unmodified tree: `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` rc 0, `FIXTURE ok: 14 error(s) pin the 931dffe acceptance (9 required)`. Perturbation: prepend 14 comment lines to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py (a `return` at line 1138 moves to 1152, inside the +-1 window checkPathLine reads) -> rc 1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: 931dffe acceptance pins missing`. Prepending 1 line instead leaves it rc 0, so the fixture is not simply shift-sensitive: it needs the cited line NOT to sit near a `return`, which any unrelated production edit above it can change. #2066's new property in thermal_model.py did exactly this.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust 1138/1152: they are measured at 47b083b0 and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. At your merge base, list `grep -n '\breturn\b' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py` near line 1152, prepend (1152 - n) comment lines for the nearest `return` at line n above it, run `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs`, and confirm whether it still goes VACUOUS; restore the file afterwards.
carries.brief: The D11 round, or whichever seat next edits tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs: stop REQUIRED_931DFFE's `wood_share:1152` pin depending on the live line layout of custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py, so an unrelated production edit cannot turn `briefs` red. Candidate repairs, to be chosen with the control: point the fixture's citation at a file the fixture owns, or have the pin assert the lookup's refusal reason rather than the production line. Demonstrate it by rerunning the 14-line prepend above: before the repair rc 1, after it rc 0, and a deliberately wrong citation must still produce the ERROR. Do not make prepr.sh run brief_lint on every production diff instead; it took 1 m 45 s under load on 47b083b0 for this one fixture.

carries.from: RCA stale-pins review (PR #2073, round 1, reviewer observation on #2070): CI never runs a round instrument's `--perturb` arm, so an instrument under dev/audit/rounds/ that a production move breaks turns nothing red
carries.control: Established at origin/main 47b083b0 by search, with a null control, not by reproducing #2070's breakage. `git grep -n -e '--perturb' -- .github` returns no line, while `git grep -n -e '--perturb' -- dev/audit | wc -l` returns 1704, so no workflow step invokes a perturbation arm. The null control is that CI does run some round instruments: `.github/workflows/governance.yml` line 411 runs `codeowners_gap.py --self-test`, so the absence above is specific to `--perturb`, not to round instruments in general. Not measured here: which round instruments broke on #2070's move of `_on_off_service`.
carries.remeasure: At your merge base rerun both `git grep` commands, and list what `--perturb` arms exist with `git grep -l -e '--perturb' -- 'dev/audit/rounds/*.py'`. A workflow that has since added a perturb runner makes the first command non-empty, and this carry is void for the arms it runs.
carries.brief: The D11 or D13 round: decide whether CI should run a round's `--perturb` arms, or whether instruments that CI never exercises are expected to rot, and record the decision. This is a different class from the stale-pin RCA (a local predictor porting half of a CI refusal): here no detector exists at any cost. Apply the cost test first, since 1704 mentions across dev/audit means a blanket run is likely unaffordable; a per-round opt-in list is the candidate form. Do not fold it into prepr.sh's step 6d.

carries.from: the pull request fixing R9-ROW-STALE (#2111), which makes tools/audit/seat/record_row.py's `--plan` ask whether an existing row already tells the merge it records (`row_matches_merge`) rather than only whether a row exists (`has_row`), so the record-autofix beat now rewrites a stale row it previously left alone
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control at the lane's merge base 7cd5a588c, on a clean worktree of it: `--enumerate` from that tree's instrument (unchanged by the fix) and `--plan` from the fix's head. The beat's reach IS its window -- `--enumerate` reads `<last tag>..HEAD` -- so the then-last tag v6.7.17 enumerates 18 merges and plans 18 rewrites, all 18 of them stale, while the same run from v6.7.13, the window that covers the whole defect, plans 103. The 85 rows in the difference are reached by no automatic run: the tag has already moved past them and the beat always starts at the tag. The perturbation that would void it is the window itself -- a last tag at or before v6.7.13, or a beat that walked back behind its tag, makes the two counts equal -- and the other arm the two numbers separate is a plan of 0 at v6.7.13, which would say the rows were already correct rather than unreached.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base, on a worktree of origin/main: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --enumerate --since $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)` then `--plan`, and read the planned-row count; repeat with `--since v6.7.13`, the earliest tag that reaches the oldest stale row. The two counts differ by exactly the rows the beat's window cannot reach. Do not carry 18 and 85: the last tag moves with every release, and both counts are functions of main's tip and of which rows were written pre-merge. A seat that reads the two counts as equal has either re-derived the window or found that it has since widened; run the wide window before concluding either.
carries.brief: Constraint on record upkeep, and the owed action this lane leaves behind. The record-autofix beat (`tools/audit/seat/record_row.py`, driven by the `record-autofix` job) corrects ONLY the merges its tag window covers -- `--enumerate` reads `<last tag>..HEAD`, deliberately, since re-reading the whole history on every push is the cost it refuses -- so a row that went stale BEFORE the last tag is corrected by no automatic run, however correct the merge predicate now is. The next seat to do record upkeep owes one explicit run of the correction over a window that reaches the defect: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --enumerate --since v6.7.13`, then `--plan` and `--apply` with `--root` at a worktree of origin/main. Measured at 7cd5a588c that plans the 103 stale rows this lane's fix exists to correct, plus the 2 merges that carry no row at all and are written rather than rewritten, one line per file, and re-plans to 0 -- the beat's own convergence, asked for over a window wide enough to include the rows. Nothing widens the tag window on its own, so this is a precondition on the record being correct rather than a recommendation: the fix converges the record inside the window it is run over, and the rows behind the tag are corrected only when a seat asks for them.
